en.title: Congress Urged to Prioritize Accessible Housing Amid Growing Disability Advocacy
en.summary: Congress is being urged to make accessibility a priority in the nation's housing supply, emphasizing the need for homes that accommodate people with disabilities. Meanwhile, Kisharon Langdon is testing accessibility boxes with sensory and communication aids for High Holy Day services, and a 71‑year‑old disabled senior repeatedly denied boarding on an accessible bus highlights ongoing transit barriers. Additional highlights include a survey on Japan's barrier‑free progress, a quick React‑Vue accessibility guide, and a Philly woman’s advocacy after a bullet‑induced paralysis.

highlights.title: Congress must prioritize accessibility in housing supply
Kisharon Langdon pilots accessibility boxes ahead of High Holy Days
71-Year-Old Disabled Senior Repeatedly Denied Boarding on Accessible Bus After 28 Years of Use, Advocacy Group Says Such Incidents Are Not Isolated
React vs Vue Accessibility Setup: 12 Steps, 90 Min [2026]
A stray bullet paralyzed a Philly woman from the waist down. Now she surfs, teaches, and advocates for accessibility.

zh-TW.title: 國會被促優先考慮無障礙住房，殘障倡議持續升溫
zh-TW.summary: 國會被呼籲將無障礙置於國家住房供應的優先位置，以確保殘障人士能獲得適切住房。同時，Kisharon Langdon 正在試點提供感官與溝通輔助的無障礙盒子，供高聖日禮拜使用；一位71歲殘障長者連續被拒絕上無障礙巴士，凸顯持續的交通障礙。此外，日本無障礙進展調查、React‑Vue 無障礙設置快速指南，以及一位費城女子在子彈導致癱瘓後成為無障礙倡導者的故事也備受關注。
